newsitem.title: USA: SEC investigating Miami $72 mln bond deal - mayor.
newsitem.headline: SEC investigating Miami $72 mln bond deal - mayor.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has begun an investigation into the City of Miami's $72 million pension bond issue, Mayor Joe Carollo said Thursday.
"The SEC has been around," Carollo told Reuters during a break in a city commission meeting.

He would not comment on reports that SEC officials had made informal requests for documents related to the taxable revenue bonds the city issued in December 1995. Carollo referred further questions to Acting City Manager Merrett Stierheim, who did not return Reuter calls.

Bond proceeds were to be used to meet pension fund obligations and to compensate retiring workers for unused sick leave. Questions about the use of bond proceeds arose last week when trustees for the City of Miami Firefighters and Police Officers Retirement Trust Fund said $37 million of bond proceeds were unaccounted for and may have been improperly co-mingled with general fund revennues.
After investigating, Stierheim said the money had been accounted for and used properly.

"There appears to be nothing irregular about the use of these bond monies," Stierheim said in a Sept 20 memo. However, the memo criticized the use of debt to meet current pension requirements, calling it "analogous to putting second and third mortgages on one's home."

The bond documents specified that some of the bond proceeds would be used to reimburse the city's general fund for the 1995 pension fund contribution. The issue was validated in court and no objections were raised during the appeals period that preceeded the sale.
The senior manager for the offering was Howard Gary & Co, which is also the city's financial adviser.
SEC District Director Charles Senatore declined to comment.
